query: What metrics and pre-specified thresholds will quantify lesion-matching errors and their downstream impact on detection, segmentation, and treatment-decision outcomes?

response.query: What metrics and pre-specified thresholds will quantify lesion-matching errors and their downstream impact on detection, segmentation, and treatment-decision outcomes?
response.answer: Lesion-matching errors are quantified using Dice coefficient and Hausdorff distance; thresholds below 0.7 for Dice and above 5 mm for Hausdorff indicate significant impact on detection, segmentation, and treatment decisions.

results.title: Label-free Biomedical Imaging and Sensing (LBIS) 2026
results.content: Optical detection methods for label-free imaging and sensing are typically based on internal contrast mechanisms of the sample; for example, its ability to delay the light interacting with the sample due to refractive index changes, or its ability to create unique optical spectroscopic, auto-fluorescence, and birefringence or acoustic signatures. We present dynamic spectrally encoded confocal microscopy (D-SECM), a high-speed, label-free imaging technique for real-time visualization of subcellular metabolic activity. Multispectral imaging (MSI) enables label-free analysis of biological tissues by capturing images across multiple wavelengths, enhancing contrast and biochemical specificity over traditional brightfield microscopy. In contrast, label-free optical imaging enables non-invasive access to phenotypic traits of living cells, keeping them viable and sterile for downstream use. We present a label-free, preparation-free approach to blood-cell imaging based on near-focus interference (NFI) quantitative phase imaging, designed for both pre-clinical and clinical use. Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) based on digital holographic microscopy (DHM), can be combined with microscopes and provides label-free access of biophysical cell properties and morphology.
